text:
maria: Heads-up - saw a reproducible perf regression on INT8 conv-deconv workload on p4d. Latency p95 jumped ~22% after the fp8/quant patch. Ran an nsys timeline, looks like tons of tiny kernel launches and a big chunk of time in a `dequantize` kernel.

maria: nsys capture command I used:
```
nsys profile --output=/tmp/trace_q1 --trace=cuda,osrt -f true 
  --sample=none --force-overwrite 
  --capture-range=cudaApi 
  python run_inference.py --model rwd-deconv-int8 --batching=auto
```

maria: timeline top lines (abridged):
```
GPU 0 | 00:00:00.001 | deq_int8_to_fp32         | duration 36.2 ms | launches 120
GPU 0 | 00:00:00.038 | matmul_small_kern        | duration 8.9 ms  | launches 310
GPU 0 | 00:00:00.047 | conv_fwd_int8            | duration 6.5 ms  | launches 95
Host  | 00:00:00.054 | cudaMemcpyAsync pinned   | duration 2.2 ms  | frequent
```

maria: Observations: deq kernel is surprisingly heavy (36ms total over short run), but more importantly we see lots of short matmul launches (~9ms) which suggests batching heuristics are fragmenting requests. There's also periodic host->device memcpy pinned ops correlated with KV cache misses.

maria: cc @tj @anika — could the new quant path be forcing dequant on the device per op instead of fusing it earlier? Also maybe our batching cutoff for deconv is suboptimal for short sequences.

tj: Thanks for the dump. Quick thought: last change added a per-op `dequant` call in the CUDA graph capture path to simplify memory views. That could avoid host copies normally, but if graph capture is disabled it becomes repeated launches.

anika: if graph capture falls back we might be losing kernel fusion. Are these runs with warmup (graph built) or cold start?

maria: Cold starts. I deliberately disabled warmup to stress small-batch latency for PLG flows. Reproduces even with single-request bursts.

sam: Could be two independent issues: 1) dequant not fused -> extra kernel cost, 2) batching heuristic picks tiny batches because latency SLOs prioritized, so we get many launches. For 1) maybe move dequant earlier into pre-packed weight buffers (quant->packed_fp16) or do dequant in host pinned buffer once per KV miss.

perf-bot: Automated analysis: kernel `deq_int8_to_fp32` accounts for 54% of GPU time in this capture. Kernel launch overhead (cudaLaunch) shows 310 short launches <10ms. High launch density correlates with >15% perf regression vs baseline.

anika: Nice. For experiments: (A) enable graph capture during cold start to see impact (B) bump batching window from 4ms->8ms to allow more accumulation, (C) change dequant from elementwise kernel to batched staging in pinned memory then single device upload.

maria: I'm going to try A/B now. Quick patch idea: when `quant_mode==int8 && graph_capture_disabled` set quant path to allocate `dequant_scratch` in pinned host and do one memcpy per KV fetch instead of launching per-op dequant kernels.

tj: Also check kernel selection heuristics: if matmul_small_kern is being used maybe it picks a non-vectorized path for small M/N. Could we prefer blocked int8 GEMMs when sequence length > threshold?

sam: I have a microbenchmark that exercises that selector. I'll run with the same capture and share numbers. Might be able to add a fast path: if batch_count<3, route to fused deq+matmul single kernel compiled for small batch.

maria: Results from quick A/B tests:
- A (graph capture enabled): p95 down 14%, deq kernel almost disappears from timeline (graph fuses it into matmul).
- B (batch window 8ms): p95 down 6% vs baseline (reduced launch density).

maria: So fusion via graph capture is the biggest win but we can't force graph capture for all customers. Need a fallback for capture-disabled environments.

anika: Good data. Next steps: sam to prototype fused deq+matmul kernel for small batches, tj to add heuristic to prefer blocked GEMM when seq_len crosses threshold, maria to implement pinned-host staging fallback for dequant on KV miss. We'll re-run nsys traces after each change.

deploy-bot: @maria scheduled test cluster job rwd-int8-debug-77 (p4d, 8 GPUs) - started 1772105600

maria: Thanks all — I'll drop the full nsys .qdrep and perf-bot flame graphs into the perf-ticket #1762. Short term mitigation: enable graph capture for our PLG default on compatible drivers and add config flag for `quant_dequant_staging=host_pinned`.

sam: FYI I saw slight accuracy delta when fusing deq->matmul for INT8 on some layernorm-adjacent ops; we should add unit evals to track any regressions from fused kernels (small tolerances).

maria: Agreed. We'll gate release on unit eval pass + perf gain.

tj: Ping me when you have the microbenchmark results, I can help update kernel selector policy.

maria: Will do. Leaving trace link here: s3://rwd-perf/traces/1772104321_qdrep.qdrep

maria: TL;DR: dequant kernel + high launch density from batching heuristics are primary causes. Graph capture fuses away most overhead; fallback is pinned staging + fused small-batch kernels.
